text: This guy paid a king $9.5 million for drilling rights in empty desert and became the richest man in America. Meet Jay Paul Getty. In 1930, Paul is a millionaire oil man and his father has just died. He leaves Paul only $500,000 of his $10 million fortune because he doesn't trust his Playboy son. So Paul sets out to prove he can do better than his father. By then, the depression has crashed oil shares and everyone is selling. But Paul's rule is to buy when everyone else is scared. So he starts buying tidewater, a giant oil company, at $2 a share to take it over. It's boss's fight for years to keep him out. But Paul is willing to wait as long as it takes. And he wins control. By 1949, tidewater is growing fast and needs more oil. There's a strip of desert between Saudi Arabia and Kuwait where nobody has ever found a drop. But it's next to a giant oil field. Big oil companies make careful offers. Paul offers the king $9.5 million, plus $1 million a year whether he finds oil or not. And twice what anyone else pays per barrel, oil men are shocked. It's a huge risk. And for three years, his wells come up dry and he spends $30 million. But he keeps drilling. And in 1953, they finally strike a giant oil field. Soon it's pumping 100,000 barrels a day. And in 1957, fortune names get the richest man in America, with a net worth over $8 billion in today's money.
